  "evidence_refs": ["Original request, S1–S2"],
  "headline": "Intake established the browser game outcome, technical boundaries, and discovery defaults.",
  "outcome": "done",
  "summary": "S1 — Fact: deliver a small single-player Battleship game playable in a browser against a computer opponent; the browser is the user entry point and the player is the consumer. Assumption: a local browser and server are the initial usable target, authorized by the request; the outcome becomes usable there after implementation and is visible in the isolated source checkout at final return; a deployed outcome exists only after release. Recorded defaults: one anonymous player per game, no account or identity tracking, game state confined to that game and discarded when it ends or the session is lost, no sharing across people, devices, or sessions, and opponent ship positions hidden until revealed by play; these defaults rule out persistence, multiplayer, and cross-device continuation. Open question for discovery: establish the available runtime and any existing workspace conventions first, then determine game rules, interaction details, state ownership, session lifetime, and what the runtime already supplies; this blocks final interaction and state design. Risk: hidden opponent state must remain concealed from the player. S2 — Fact: use a Node.js server and include tests. Open question for discovery: establish the available Node.js runtime and tooling first, then select the server and test setup; this blocks implementation and test execution. Run boundary: intake only, with no implementation; the repository is empty. Source hints: no team, workspace channels, internal sites or docs, private repositories, owners, or ambiguous domain terms were supplied; discovery may inspect available workspace and runtime evidence. Authority boundary: the request grants delivery to the named browser target; no separate deployment target or release is specified."
}
